detail.problem_context: In vivo protein-RNA interactions are mapped almost exclusively by CLIP-seq, which profiles one protein in one cell type per experiment and needs a specific antibody; only about 10% of the roughly 2,000 human RNA-binding proteins have been assayed, and the Protein Data Bank holds around 5,000 protein-RNA complexes, a quarter of them ribosomes.
detail.method_architecture: Sequence-based prediction could extend coverage to unprofiled, newly discovered, or designed molecules, but existing predictors are not built for that case. One family trains a separate model per protein and cannot move beyond proteins with CLIP data; the other scores pairs but targets a single RNA class.
detail.findings_tradeoffs: Most are evaluated with random splits and randomly paired negatives that leave near-identical sequences on both sides of the split, and many require structure or read only short windows, discarding the context around a binding site. Their accuracy falls sharply when whole molecules are held out. We address this with two contributions. First, a strict benchmark of 2.1 million examples built from 11.6 million peaks of CLIP experiments targeting 209 proteins, taken from four public databases, in which each RNA is a spliced transcript with nucleotide-level labels, and sequence-similarity clusters are assigned whole to training, validation, and test sets, giving separate slices for unseen RNAs, unseen proteins, and unseen pairs. Negatives are matched to positives in length and in the number of other proteins binding the transcript, removing the shortcut by which a model predicts binding from how popular a transcript is without reading the protein. Second, RPI-Zero, a sequence-only model that reads any full-length protein and RNA jointly in up to 4,096 tokens, so the RNA representation is conditioned on the protein, and describes every protein as a mixture of shared motif prototypes, placing unseen proteins in the same terms as training ones. One model covers all proteins and RNA classes, uses no structure, and needs no interaction data for a new molecule. Compared with five state-of-the-art methods, it achieves the highest score in eight different metrics on unseen RNAs, unseen proteins, and unseen pairs. The model and data are available at https://github.com/ciceklab/RPI-Zero and https://zenodo.org/records/23748141, respectively.

items.headline: FoldAbS: Repurposing the Protein Folding Model as a Foundation Encoder for Antibody Screening
items.summary: Therapeutic antibody screening requires prioritizing antibody candidates across specificity, affinity, and developability. Current pipelines typically silo these objectives and underuse structural information that governs antibody-antigen recognition. To address these inefficacies, we introduce FoldAbS, a unified supervised screening framework that reconceptualizes protein folding models as frozen foundation encoders, exploiting their internal representations to capture rich sequence, geometric, and interaction dynamics well beyond basic structure prediction.

detail.abstract_excerpt: Therapeutic antibody screening requires prioritizing antibody candidates across specificity, affinity, and developability. Current pipelines typically silo these objectives and underuse structural information that governs antibody-antigen recognition. To address these inefficacies, we introduce FoldAbS, a unified supervised screening framework that reconceptualizes protein folding models as frozen foundation encoders, exploiting their internal representations to capture rich sequence, geometric, and interaction dynamics well beyond basic structure prediction. By coupling the folding model with lightweight, task-specific heads, FoldAbS seamlessly evaluates all three therapeutic criteria within a single architecture. Instantiating this framework with the open-source Protenix model (FoldAbS-Px) yields consistent improvements over baseline approaches, achieving significant performance gains of up to 13.1%, 9.2%, and 6.2% in specificity, affinity, and developability, respectively. Collectively, these results reposition protein folding models from structure predictors and confidence scorers into reusable foundation encoders for comprehensive and supervised antibody screening. Our code is available at https://github.com/nohandsomewujun/FoldAbS.

items.headline: Beyond Instruction Override: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injection with Task-Tampering Attacks
items.summary: Indirect prompt-injection (IPI) benchmarks predominantly test planted instructions that redirect a tool-using agent toward an attacker-chosen task. Yet attacker-controlled content can instead tamper with the outcome of the task already in progress. A buyer's dispute evidence can cite a false refund policy to inflate a refund without changing the task.

detail.problem_context: Indirect prompt-injection (IPI) benchmarks predominantly test planted instructions that redirect a tool-using agent toward an attacker-chosen task.
detail.method_architecture: Yet attacker-controlled content can instead tamper with the outcome of the task already in progress. A buyer's dispute evidence can cite a false refund policy to inflate a refund without changing the task.
detail.findings_tradeoffs: We define IPI by authority rather than instruction-like wording: planted content constitutes an attack when it attempts to influence a decision that its source is not authorized to determine. We introduce a benchmark that makes this boundary explicit: in each of 90 validated cases across three tool-use environments, the user request specifies the source that resolves the targeted decision. Every attack tampers with a decision required by the benign task rather than replacing that task. Each case has attacks with the same harmful outcome that target up to six parts of the agent's decision making: its objective, decision rules, available actions, expected consequences, reading of observations, or beliefs about the current state. Without a defense, attacks on three of the five other targets (decision rules, available actions, and state) have higher mean success than objective attacks across five LLMs. A detection-and-removal defense reduces objective-targeting attacks to 2.4% success but leaves observation- and state-targeting attacks at 9.5% and 12.1%; this gap persists under detection-optimized rewrites. A tool-policy defense still allows 15.4% attack success, close to 17.0% without a defense, because these attacks generally retain expected tools and manipulate values obtained during execution. Evaluations whose attacks redirect the task or target only the agent's objective can therefore overestimate the coverage of these defenses. Code and data are available at https://github.com/amazon-science/task-tampering-prompt-injection.

items.headline: Stop Calling Them Provers: The Case for Calling ProVerif and Tamarin Symbolic Protocol Analyzers
items.summary: A claim that a cryptographic protocol has been proved secure depends on the theory, the analysis software, the protocol model, and the security property being checked. I examine each of these for ProVerif and Tamarin. An audit of their published soundness arguments finds false statements, missing proofs, and gaps between the procedures justified on paper and those the tools run.

detail.problem_context: A claim that a cryptographic protocol has been proved secure depends on the theory, the analysis software, the protocol model, and the security property being checked.
detail.method_architecture: I examine each of these for ProVerif and Tamarin. An audit of their published soundness arguments finds false statements, missing proofs, and gaps between the procedures justified on paper and those the tools run.
detail.findings_tradeoffs: I also reproduce previously reported bugs that cause Tamarin to accept false claims about the submitted models. ProVerif supplies no certificate for its full analysis, while Tamarin replays its proof tree with its own solver, leaving the correctness of that code to be trusted. A correct symbolic result can still fall short of the security claim made for a protocol. Models can omit behavior in parsers and state machines; secrecy queries can allow information to leak; and equations for cryptographic primitives need justification before they support computational guarantees. Better models, stronger queries and computational soundness arguments can address these problems, but someone must establish that they apply to the protocol at hand. For these reasons and more, I argue that calling ProVerif and Tamarin "provers" is misleading: we should call them symbolic protocol analyzers and report their results with the models, assumptions and evidence that support them. They remain useful for finding attacks and establishing symbolic properties, including for unbounded sessions.

items.headline: Practical Optimal Bucket Sets with Power-of-Two Radices for LFG-Based MSM Algorithms
items.summary: Fixed point multi-scalar multiplication (MSM) is a major computational component of pairing-based SNARK proof generation. The Luo--Fu--Gong (LFG) framework is a variant of Pippenger's bucket method that uses a multiplier set $M$ and precomputed point multiples to reduce the number of buckets and online point additions. For radix $q$ and a positive multiplier set $M$, covering all digit residues requires a bucket set of size at least $q/(2|M|)$.

detail.problem_context: Fixed point multi-scalar multiplication (MSM) is a major computational component of pairing-based SNARK proof generation.
detail.method_architecture: The Luo--Fu--Gong (LFG) framework is a variant of Pippenger's bucket method that uses a multiplier set $M$ and precomputed point multiples to reduce the number of buckets and online point additions. For radix $q$ and a positive multiplier set $M$, covering all digit residues requires a bucket set of size at least $q/(2|M|)$.
detail.findings_tradeoffs: Previous constructions approaching this bound based on primitive roots or power-residue classes impose radix restrictions that exclude $q=2^c$, thereby requiring additional binary-to-radix conversion in software implementations. We present two main bucket set constructions for power-of-two radices $q=2^c$, using the multiplier sets $M=\{1,2,3\}$ and $M=\{1,3\}$, respectively. Their cardinalities are $q/6+O(\log q)$ and $q/4+2$, respectively, so both asymptotically attain the counting bound $q/(2|M|)$ while allowing efficient radix-digit extraction through shifts and masks. We further give two generalizations. Using consecutive powers of $3$ as multipliers yields bucket sets of size $q/(2\ell)+O(\log q)$ for every fixed positive integer $\ell$. For $\ell=2^d$ and $c\ge d+2$, consecutive odd multipliers yield bucket sets of size $q/(2\ell)+d+1$. We also present scalar conversion and two strategies for handling the leading digit, allowing the bucket set constructions to be used within the LFG framework.

items.headline: MuCPay: Breaking the Quadratic Bottleneck in Scriptless Multi-Party Oracle-Based Conditional Payments
items.summary: Oracle-based conditional payments triggered by real-world events support decentralized finance applications. However, dense independent bilateral deployments require $\Theta(Nn^2)$ outcome authorizations and $\Theta(n^2)$ settlement signatures for $n$ parties and $N$ outcomes. To go beyond two-party settings, we propose MuCPay, a multi-party oracle-based conditional payment protocol combining (i) $\Theta(Nn)$ off-chain signing shares with one on-chain settlement signature and (ii) BIP340-compatible scriptless settlement on Bitcoin.
items.headline_tr: MuCPay: Komut Dosyası Olmayan Çok Taraflı Oracle Tabanlı Koşullu Ödemelerde İkinci Dereceden Darboğazı Aşmak
items.summary_tr: Gerçek dünyadaki olayların tetiklediği Oracle tabanlı koşullu ödemeler, merkezi olmayan finans uygulamalarını destekler. Bununla birlikte, yoğun bağımsız ikili konuşlandırmalar, $n$ taraflar ve $N$ sonuçlar için $\Theta(Nn^2)$ sonuç yetkilerini ve $\Theta(n^2)$ uzlaşma imzalarını gerektirir. İki partili ayarların ötesine geçmek için, çok partili oracle tabanlı bir con olan MuCPay'i öneriyoruz.

detail.problem_context: Oracle-based conditional payments triggered by real-world events support decentralized finance applications.
detail.method_architecture: However, dense independent bilateral deployments require $\Theta(Nn^2)$ outcome authorizations and $\Theta(n^2)$ settlement signatures for $n$ parties and $N$ outcomes. To go beyond two-party settings, we propose MuCPay, a multi-party oracle-based conditional payment protocol combining (i) $\Theta(Nn)$ off-chain signing shares with one on-chain settlement signature and (ii) BIP340-compatible scriptless settlement on Bitcoin.
detail.findings_tradeoffs: At its core, MuCPay introduces hash-bound adaptor multi-signatures (HB-AMS) that aggregate parties' conditional authorizations into a compact joint pre-signature. Its single-nonce structure and hash-bound adaptor integration enable efficient multi-party pre-signing. items.headline: Fully Homomorphic Encryption: A Mathematical Introduction
items.summary: We provide a mathematical introduction to fully homomorphic encryption (FHE), which enables computations to be performed on encrypted data without requiring decryption. We begin with a brief overview of the historical development of FHE, then focus on Fully Homomorphic Encryption over the Torus (TFHE), describing its underlying mathematical structure and fundamental homomorphic operations. Particular attention is given to key switching and bootstrapping, including their roles in managing ciphertext noise and supporting computations of greater depth.

items.headline: Can Home Visits Re-Engage Chronically Absent Students? Evidence from the LEAP Program -- by Eric Brunner, Shangyue Jiang, Stephen Ross
items.summary: Beginning in the summer of 2021, the state of Connecticut launched the Learner Engagement and Attendance Program (LEAP) where home visits by school personnel were conducted with students identified as chronically absent from Connecticut’s 15 most disadvantaged school districts. Home visits were designed to connect students and their families directly with teachers to foster strong connections. We use student-level data from 2021–22 through 2023-24 to estimate event studies of the effect of LEAP on student attendance, chronic absenteeism, disciplinary incidents, and student achievement.

items.headline: Unraveling the Cobweb of Global Imbalances: Drivers, Vulnerabilities and Adjustment Scenarios -- by Stefan Avdjiev, Kristin Forbes, Tsvetelina Nenova, Marjorie Santos
items.summary: This paper analyses the evolution and drivers of the stock of global imbalances in order to assess associated vulnerabilities and potential adjustment scenarios. These imbalances have recently increased sharply, with a deterioration in the US net international investment position (NIIP) mirrored by NIIP improvements in most other major economies. We decompose these NIIP changes into their proximate drivers for a sample of 28 economies and find that financial factors (including valuation changes and investment income flows) are the primary drivers of global imbalances at both short and long horizons, while trade also plays a significant role (especially at long horizons).

We study the relative productivity of workers benefiting from an aggressive affirmative action policy in a setting where hiring constraints are mandated upon employers and are typically likely to bind. In India, colleges are required to reserve approximately 50 percent of faculty hires for individuals from disadvantaged caste and social class groups. We collect and analyze data from a nationally representative sample of 50 engineering and technology colleges in India, some of which randomly assign students to classrooms. We find that reservation category faculty have lower levels of education, lower professorial ranks and fewer years of experience in academia than general category faculty who are not hired through reservations. Yet, even with lower qualifications, we do not detect meaningful differences in instructional quality between reservation category faculty and general category faculty across a wide range of measures that include course grades, follow-on course grades, standardized test scores, dropout, attendance, graduate school plans, and graduation. Furthermore, even in the face of potential discrimination and resentment against faculty hiring quotas, general category students perform slightly better in classrooms taught by reservation category faculty than general category faculty. Finally, estimates of differences between reservation category and general category faculty in several measures of research productivity and administrative service are small in magnitude and not statistically different from zero. The findings have implications for the heated debates over affirmative action programs found in many countries around the world and in India which is now the largest country in the world.

items.headline: Saving for the Machines -- by Jesús Fernández-Villaverde
items.summary: When machines can perform a growing share of tasks, growth depends on two margins: how the task structure affects the returns to accumulating machines, and how strongly capital accumulation responds to those returns. I argue that, in a standard task model, capital supply governs the size of the growth boom associated with automation, while the task structure sets the duration of this growth boom and the evolution of wages. I document how the same technology path that generates 11.7% annual growth when households choose their saving rate optimally delivers only 2.2% when the saving rate is fixed at the calibrated U.S.

I document how the same technology path that generates 11.7% annual growth when households choose their saving rate optimally delivers only 2.2% when the saving rate is fixed at the calibrated U.S.
detail.findings_tradeoffs: 2025 level of 23%. Therefore, slow growth might reflect too little capital accumulation instead of a technological bottleneck. Also, the saving rate rises mainly because automation raises the capital share, not because households become thriftier. Long yields price the growth boom: the ten-year real yield jumps from 5.1% to 13.6% on impact. In my benchmark calibration, hand-to-mouth households lose the equivalent of two-fifths to two-thirds of their consumption, while keeping them on trend temporarily costs at most a fifth of GDP.

detail.abstract_excerpt: When machines can perform a growing share of tasks, growth depends on two margins: how the task structure affects the returns to accumulating machines, and how strongly capital accumulation responds to those returns. I argue that, in a standard task model, capital supply governs the size of the growth boom associated with automation, while the task structure sets the duration of this growth boom and the evolution of wages. I document how the same technology path that generates 11.7% annual growth when households choose their saving rate optimally delivers only 2.2% when the saving rate is fixed at the calibrated U.S. 2025 level of 23%. Therefore, slow growth might reflect too little capital accumulation instead of a technological bottleneck. Also, the saving rate rises mainly because automation raises the capital share, not because households become thriftier. Long yields price the growth boom: the ten-year real yield jumps from 5.1% to 13.6% on impact. In my benchmark calibration, hand-to-mouth households lose the equivalent of two-fifths to two-thirds of their consumption, while keeping them on trend temporarily costs at most a fifth of GDP.

items.headline: Information Elicitation by Ordinal Agreement
items.summary: Ordinal information is central to tasks ranging from conference peer review to Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback for large language models. In many such settings, there is no objective ground truth against which reports can be directly verified, making incentive-compatible elicitation challenging. Peer-prediction mechanisms have been designed to achieve truthful elicitation despite the lack of ground-truth verification.

detail.problem_context: Ordinal information is central to tasks ranging from conference peer review to Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback for large language models.
detail.method_architecture: In many such settings, there is no objective ground truth against which reports can be directly verified, making incentive-compatible elicitation challenging. Peer-prediction mechanisms have been designed to achieve truthful elicitation despite the lack of ground-truth verification.
detail.findings_tradeoffs: However, existing peer-prediction methods do not provide incentives for agents to truthfully compress rich private information (e.g. reviews) into coarser ordinal reports (e.g. rankings) requested by the mechanisms. We propose a simple ordinal peer-prediction mechanism that rewards agents based on pairwise agreement, measured by Kendall tau. Under a broad class of Bayesian Stochastically Order Consistent models---which includes classical models such as Mallows and Thurstone---we prove that truthful reporting is stochastically dominant, and strongly truthful under index-equivariant strategies. This provides robust incentives even for agents with non-linear utility functions, such as risk aversion. Our mechanism further accommodates heterogeneous agents, top-K reports, and subset assignments, where each agent is scored against one randomly drawn peer. Experiments on synthetic Mallows and Thurstone data, together with a real-data stress test on the SUSHI preference dataset, show right-shifted truthful-payment distributions and the highest normalized sensitivity among tested baselines.

items.headline: A Sequential Framework for Urban Drone Delivery: Network Design, Vehicle Sizing, and Energy and Cost Assessment
items.summary: A sequential engineering framework is presented for urban drone delivery, linking hub location, route planning, mission-specific vehicle sizing, and energy and operating cost assessment. Aggregate origin-destination demand is assumed known a priori. For each hub configuration, the maximum required link distance is minimized, and feasible routes that return to their departure hubs are generated.

detail.problem_context: A sequential engineering framework is presented for urban drone delivery, linking hub location, route planning, mission-specific vehicle sizing, and energy and operating cost assessment.
detail.method_architecture: Aggregate origin-destination demand is assumed known a priori. For each hub configuration, the maximum required link distance is minimized, and feasible routes that return to their departure hubs are generated.
detail.findings_tradeoffs: Route frequencies are determined using mixed-integer linear programming to satisfy delivery demand. The resulting range requirement guides motor-propeller selection and battery sizing to minimize vehicle takeoff mass. Flight distances and frequencies, cruise performance, and vehicle dimensions are combined to estimate monthly energy consumption, fleet size, hub area, staffing, and operating cost. The framework is applied to district-level Seoul delivery data. Increasing the number of hubs from one to four reduces the required range from 30.6 to 21.9 km and vehicle takeoff mass from 8.12 to 6.12 kg. Despite a 21.5% increase in total flight distance, monthly flight energy consumption decreases by 13.1%, from 15.2 to 13.2 MWh. Battery replacement is the largest vehicle-related operating expense, while operating cost per delivery increases from USD 1.18 to USD 2.20 because of higher rent and labor costs at the hubs. Among the designs evaluated, range-matched vehicles achieve the lowest operating cost in the two- and four-hub networks; a longer-range vehicle is least costly in the three-hub network. Sensitivity analyses further examine the effects of delivery demand and operating assumptions. The results demonstrate that reductions in vehicle mass and energy consumption do not necessarily lead to lower system operating cost.

items.headline: Solvable macroscopic models for populations of type I excitability neurons with Gaussian noise
items.summary: The dynamics of type I excitability neurons near the bifurcation point are governed by the model of quadratic integrate-and-fire neuron (QIF). The model of QIF subject to white Gaussian noise is abundant in statistical physics, since it not only reasonably reproduces the dynamics of some biological systems but also emerges in the problems of stochastic stability and in quantum mechanics of one-dimensional systems with quenched disorder. We derive the solution for the mean interspike interval of a QIF subject to additive Gaussian noise in terms of analytic functions, from the first passage time problem.
items.headline_tr: Gauss gürültüsüne sahip tip I uyarılabilirlik nöronlarının popülasyonları için çözülebilir makroskopik modeller
items.summary_tr: Çatallanma noktasına yakın tip I uyarılabilirlik nöronlarının dinamikleri, ikinci dereceden entegre etme ve ateşleme nöronu (QIF) modeli tarafından yönetilir. Beyaz Gauss gürültüsüne maruz kalan QIF modeli, istatistiksel fizikte bol miktarda bulunur, çünkü yalnızca bazı biyolojik sistemlerin dinamiklerini makul bir şekilde yeniden üretmekle kalmaz, aynı zamanda stokastik kararlılık problemlerinde de ortaya çıkar.

items.headline: Distributed Optimization Involving Non-Lipschitzian, Linear Composite Functions: Unified Algorithm Design and Convergence Analysis
items.summary: This paper formulates a generic distributed nonsmooth optimization problem subject to edge-based equality constraints, local inequality constraints characterized by general convex functions, as well as globally coupling constraints including affine equality and nonlinear inequality. The terminal goal is to minimize the sum of local non-differentiable convex functions and proximable nonsmooth convex composite terms attached to linear operators, over networked multi-agent systems. items.headline: Vibration patterns and reed - pipe coupling in the free reeds of the hulusi
items.summary: The hulusi is a free-reed instrument from Yunnan, Western China, known for its unique sound. Its reed and frame are cut from a single brass sheet in a symmetric shape, the free end narrower than the clamped end. Its free reeds are coupled to tubes that determine the instrument's pitch during normal playing.

detail.findings_tradeoffs: With reduced playing pressure, the reed frequency takes over the instrument sound. We report point-by-point laser Doppler vibrometry on the reeds of six handmade hulusi, two each in the keys of F, B$\flat$ and C, measured at 29 points on every reed or tongue over nine fingerings and two supply pressures. Steady-state spectra carry two components: a tube-dominant frequency $f_\mathrm{tube}$, locked to the air-column resonance and carrying a complete harmonic series, and a reed-dominant frequency $f_\mathrm{reed}$, which is not an integer multiple of it. Their difference $Δ= f_\mathrm{tube} - f_\mathrm{reed}$ runs from 38 to 523~Hz across the dataset, from about three semitones to more than an octave. The reed-dominant frequency rises with the pressure at the reed, by $28.0 \pm 10.3$ Hz/kPa once $f_\mathrm{tube}$ is controlled for. At low pressure supply the oscillation loses its lock to the air column, falls silent for about 100~ms, and returns at the reed frequency within 0.1 Hz. The spatial patterns are forced oscillation shapes of one limit cycle at its fundamental and harmonics rather than eigenmodes: the measured frequencies stand in strict 1:2:3 ratios, far from the bending ratios of a cantilever. The reed-dominant pattern is pure bending and holds across fingerings and supply pressures, whereas the tube-dominant pattern breaks up near the oscillation threshold.

items.headline: Evolutionary dynamics of collective-risk social dilemma game with risk uncertainty and adaptive strategy
items.summary: The collective-risk dilemma game constitutes the leading metaphor for studying the evolution of cooperation in populations of selfish individuals. Although most theoretical studies often consider the risk level as a fixed parameter, this may not fully reflect the uncertain nature of risk detected in real-world scenarios. Motivated by the observation that individuals can infer their game environment and accordingly adjust their actual behavior, here we investigate this game with uncertain risk.

detail.findings_tradeoffs: In particular, we introduce a type of adaptive agents who incur an observation cost to infer the risk level during game interactions, and subsequently decide whether to cooperate or defect based on their tolerance thresholds. We first calculate the fixation probabilities of three different strategies in a mutation-free regime. Our results show that adaptive agents are favored by natural selection at low observation costs and moderate tolerance thresholds. Moreover, the fixation of adaptive agents results in higher levels of cooperation when both parameters are relatively low. We then consider behavioral mutation and systematically explore how average cooperation level and group achievement vary with observation costs, tolerance thresholds, and mutation rates. Importantly, the main results remain intact when the mutation is considered. Furthermore, when the tolerance threshold is small, the presence of adaptive agents results in a higher cooperation level and group achievement compared to the traditional setup when only unconditional cooperators and defectors are present. This advantage, however, gradually erodes with an increasing tolerance threshold and these two quantities fall below the levels observed in the classic two-strategy case.

items.headline: Learning and Steering in Incomplete-Information Games
items.summary: In many modern multi-agent systems, a mediator seeks to influence strategic decision dynamics using only outcome-level feedback and without knowing agents' utilities. In this work, we study how a mediator can learn an unknown game and steer adaptive agents toward outcomes that maximize her utility using only trajectory feedback. The mediator knows the game form and her own objective, but not the agents' utilities.

We further show that the approximation factor $2+1/k$ is asymptotically tight for our main algorithm. We also construct a four-agent, ten-chore instance in which every complete allocation has EFX approximation factor at least $11/10$, improving upon the $20/19$ lower bound for submodular costs even under additive costs.

items.headline: Current frontiers in mobility and well-being
items.summary: Human mobility has a profound impact on social structure and collective behavior, which allows individuals to reshape group structures in response to strategy information, acting as a double-edged sword for cooperative behavior. It can both disrupt existing cooperative communities and enable individuals to escape adverse environments and seek high-quality interaction partners. This paper surveys current research progress on the impact of mobility on cooperation within the framework of evolutionary game theory, focusing on specific mechanisms of passive escape, dynamic self-organization driven by active choice, and the core trade-off between migration costs and speed.

detail.findings_tradeoffs: Mobility, an individual's spatial response to local strategic information that turns location into strategic advantage, influences cooperative evolution by altering interactive information and environmental feedback, consequently affecting sustainable social well-being, such as collective benefits. Under specific conditions, this self-interested behavior at the individual level can foster macrosocial harmony, embodying the unity of individual rationality and collective cooperation. Furthermore, we also discusses inter-layer migration and information routing mechanisms in multilayer networks and extends the perspective to human-machine hybrid systems where mobile agents with information regulation capabilities can serve as information supernodes. Our paper aims to provide a unified framework for understanding mobility as a combined physical and informational driving force in the evolution of cooperation.

The United States leads the world in the sophistication and power of its artificial intelligence models, and its innovation base and investment in research and development remain unparalleled.But AI competition is much broader than modeling alone. It encompasses a technology ecosystem that includes power generation, servers, and deployment in real-world applications. Jensen Huang, co-founder and CEO of Nvidia, has described the AI industry as a five-layer cake with energy at its base and chips, infrastructure, models, and applications above it. To win the AI race with China, the United States needs to maintain or establish an advantage in each of these layers. And to do that, the United States needs Taiwan.
